req.title: Password hashing uses generate_password_hash
req.statement: The system shall store passwords via werkzeug generate_password_hash rather than plaintext.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-035 mandates that passwords are stored via werkzeug's generate_password_hash rather than plaintext. Tests must verify: (1) positive — registration succeeds and the stored password is a werkzeug hash (not plaintext); (2) negative — plaintext password is NOT stored in the database; (3) boundary — the hash stored is verifiable by check_password_hash, confirming the correct hashing algorithm is used end-to-end. Additional tests cover state transitions (login succeeds after registration, proving the hash round-trips correctly) and decision-table coverage (wrong password rejected, correct password accepted).

tests.name: test_password_stored_as_hash_not_plaintext
actions: Query the database directly for the stored password of 'testuser_ep'
expected: Stored password field does NOT equal plaintext 'mySecret123'
Stored password field starts with 'scrypt:' or 'pbkdf2:' (werkzeug hash prefix)
trace: R-FLASKR-035: passwords stored via generate_password_hash not plaintext
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'testuser_ep', 'password': 'mySecret123'})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute("SELECT password FROM user WHERE username = 'testuser_ep'").fetchone()
    assert row is not None, 'User not found in database'
    stored_pw = row['password']
    assert stored_pw != 'mySecret123', 'Password stored as plaintext!'
    assert stored_pw.startswith('scrypt:') or stored_pw.startswith('pbkdf2:'), \
        f'Unexpected hash prefix: {stored_pw[:20]}'
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_hash_verifiable_by_check_password_hash
actions: Call werkzeug check_password_hash(stored_hash, 'cloud') — must return True
Call werkzeug check_password_hash(stored_hash, 'CLOUD') — must return False (case-sensitive boundary)
expected: check_password_hash returns True for correct plaintext 'cloud'
trace: R-FLASKR-035: hash must be verifiable by check_password_hash round-trip
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db
from werkzeug.security import check_password_hash

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'testuser_bva', 'password': 'cloud'})
assert r.status_code == 302

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute("SELECT password FROM user WHERE username = 'testuser_bva'").fetchone()
    assert row is not None
    stored_pw = row['password']
    assert check_password_hash(stored_pw, 'cloud') == True, \
        'check_password_hash should return True for correct password'
    assert check_password_hash(stored_pw, 'CLOUD') == False, \
        'check_password_hash should return False for wrong-case password'
    assert check_password_hash(stored_pw, '') == False, \
        'check_password_hash should return False for empty string'
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_login_succeeds_after_hashed_registration
actions: Assert login redirects to index (hash round-trip works)
expected: Login with correct password returns HTTP 302 to /
Login with wrong password returns HTTP 200 with error message
trace: R-FLASKR-035: hash stored must allow successful login via check_password_hash
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'testuser_stc', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

r2 = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'testuser_stc', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r2.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 on correct login, got {r2.status_code}'
assert r2.headers['Location'] == '/'

r3 = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'testuser_stc', 'password': 'wrongpass'})
assert r3.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200 on bad login, got {r3.status_code}'
assert b'Incorrect password.' in r3.data
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_preloaded_user_password_is_hashed_not_plaintext
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with fixture data (user Rahul/stone, Anjali/cloud, James/river)
Passwords in DB are hashed versions of the plaintext credentials
expected: Stored password for Rahul is not 'stone'
trace: R-FLASKR-035: pre-loaded fixture users also have hashed passwords
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db
from werkzeug.security import check_password_hash

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute("SELECT password FROM user WHERE username = 'Rahul'").fetchone()
    assert row is not None
    stored_pw = row['password']
    assert stored_pw != 'stone', 'Plaintext stored for Rahul'
    assert check_password_hash(stored_pw, 'stone') == True
    assert check_password_hash(stored_pw, 'cloud') == False
    assert check_password_hash(stored_pw, 'river') == False

r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302
assert r_login.headers['Location'] == '/'
os.unlink(path)

actions: Assert hash contains ':' separator (werkzeug format requirement)
Assert hash length > 20 (not a trivially short encoding)
expected: Stored hash is not empty string
trace: R-FLASKR-035: generate_password_hash produces structured werkzeug hash

from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'testuser_fmt', 'password': 'ember'})
assert r.status_code == 302

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute("SELECT password FROM user WHERE username = 'testuser_fmt'").fetchone()
    assert row is not None
    stored_pw = row['password']
    assert stored_pw != '', 'Stored password is empty'
    assert stored_pw != 'ember', 'Stored password is plaintext'
    assert ':' in stored_pw, f'No colon separator in hash: {stored_pw[:30]}'
    assert len(stored_pw) > 20, f'Hash too short: {len(stored_pw)}'
os.unlink(path)
